comments.author: Minute-Animator-376
comments.body:
What worked for me after seeing ale the posts about three.js oneshots i asked astra to reserch why the games looks much better than made with AI in unity/godot. I had my own UI with custom tools and everything I would need with AI assisted game dev but in the end we build on top of that workflow so AI doesn't use "human" ui through mpc with unity but has its own version where it sees now all frames with all assets and objects in one place and has all the tools in this view build for AI where I have my own UIand changes made by me -  it will see them nearly in real time. I no longer need to screenshot and explain moved the codex inside unity so for example when I click an asset or mark multiple and write a prompt to AI it has all info from unity not a screenshot. Visually the game gets much better with each iteration and I don't need to go back and forth explaining. 

Bottom line: unity as game engine has "human" ui that makes sense for developer, as AI it needs to make multiple changes in diffrent parts of Ui, sometimes running diffrent mpc commands and let's say simple shader change and lighting is like 10 diffrent steps and changes that need to play together and after each change from each steps it needs to visualy verify. This takes time, burns tokens and in the end the end result is often nothing compared to a concept art. 

With modified ui and custom mpc it literally does everything now as a one-shot without extra steps and has more info than it would get from any regular mpc tools for unity. So three.js AI first workflow in unity with unity game engine that allows for complex game and ports to diffrent consoles/mobile/pc and made also my work much faster and easier as I have now everything in one UI that is also assisted by AI.

replies.author: Maximum-Substance-62
replies.body: This sounds exactly like the bottleneck I keep hitting with AI-assisted Unity development. Is your custom Unity UI/MCP something you’ve released publicly, or is it all private tooling? I’d be really interested in seeing how you’re exposing live Unity state and visual feedback to Codex without constantly feeding it screenshots and explaining context.

replies.author: Minute-Animator-376
replies.body:
Custom tool I build for myself and my game - it is probably not a one size fit all as it is for specific game and my workflow (plus I don't have a game dev background so this workaround is the best idea for my use case).

How I got to this results: 
1. While working on the game I've build my own authoring tool so I could make all the changes I wanted in one Ui with multiple tabs. Like overworld tab with live preview so I could paint over the hexes, customise biomes, create new biomes, change/replace or generate new assets using image gen through Web(sends the request to Web version and downloads the generation to unity), quests tab, enemies etc. 
2. Run a deep reaserch using 6 Pro on Web why three.js oneshots looks better than same ai working in unity/godot.
3. Ai explained why from AI view why three.js is much better for AI but long term it will cause more issues with a complex game as mine. Advised to use unity. At the end it mentioned that it can create its own authoring tool so the workflow is similar to three.js in unity. 
4. Feed the reaserch into codex with astra high asked to review the reaserch and if it is viable. Assessed as very viable, planned with astra max, then implemented with astra high.
5. Ported all plugins, functions from unity into my authoring tool and AI tool so they could stay in sync but AI has more functions (stuff I wouldn't dare to touch and would ask AI anyway)
6. It wrote custom mpc for its own tool. 
7. Asked if we can move codex and image gen directly into this tools (yep it worked)
8. Now I can modify whatever I want, mark ui, game locations, assets etc. And when I prompting the AI it has references from unity, exactl location on the map/asset/settings etc. It makes changes that I can then adjust like tweak the asset position or whatever instead burning tokens and asking AI to do something with it when I can do it myself now. 

Overall it works amazingly compared to normal mpcs I was using, worflow is now very fast with fast iterations and less usage on my weekly limits. QA is creazy fast. Currently running it with claude opus and 1400+ test cases are finished within 13s game speed run.
